changelog: Added explicit cap when a cut falls between a subject NP (proper-name/noun) and a following finite verb: lower Top -> Middle (50–70) to avoid over-trusting subject–predicate splits (addresses en_us_337).

Re-anchored trailing-comma semantics: a comma/semicolon only supports Top when the immediate pre-marker token itself is a finite verb or a clause-closing token; otherwise treat it as non-closing and cap to Middle (40–60) (addresses en_us_357 and calibration_fix).

If the immediate pre-marker token looks like a past-participle (surface -ed or a short irregular participle form), lower score into Middle/Low (20–50) because the left is likely a reduced dependent modifier (addresses en_us_1416).

Detect probable appositive/title splits: when the token after the marker is a capitalized proper name and the token before the marker is a common-noun title (e.g., 'president', 'Pharaoh'), cap to Middle (40–60) rather than Top (addresses en_us_1105).

If a comma precedes a small noun-head (numeral or determiner-less noun like 'one', 'many') that continues the previous phrase, cap score to Middle (40–60) because the right likely continues/attaches to the left (addresses en_us_548).
Updated examples to illustrate the revised punctuation, participial, and subject–verb split rules (moved the '2019,' example into Middle range and added a subject+proper-name split example).

changelog: Re-anchored the low-end calibration: reserve 0–9 for unmistakable, unrescued fragments; shift other low labels upward to reflect that many previously 00–09 items were moderate (addresses 'calibration_fix').

Introduce a two-step scoring workflow: assign an initial surface-based score, then apply bounded, conjunctive modifiers (penalties) for specific risky surface patterns observed in the critique; this targets systematic over-trust while avoiding brittle one-rule caps.

Add a conjunctive short-PP-with-trailing-comma test that strongly reduces scores only when a short adjunct (prep + ≤3-token NP) with trailing comma immediately precedes a marker and the right begins a new finite-clause — lowers to Low (floor ≤20) to fix en_us_357 style errors.

Add a conservative multi-word-name / proper-name split penalty: when the left token is capitalized and likely part of a multiword name (preceded by another capitalized token or common title), and the right begins with a finite verb, apply a moderate penalty (push toward Middle) to correct en_us_337 over-trust.

Add a targeted title+name apposition test: when the right is a single capitalized token and the left is a common-noun title or determiner+common-noun, require nearby punctuation or appositive signal before applying a moderate lowering to Middle (addresses en_us_1105) — conjunctive check avoids false positives.

Add a restricting-adverb sequence rule: when the right begins with 'only' or 'just' (case-insensitive) immediately followed by a preposition or numeral, apply a strong penalty (floor ≤10) because such tails almost always continue/limit the left (addresses en_us_1575).
Updated Decision Procedure: explicitly instruct initial assignment + ordered modifier application with caps/floors and integer rounding, to make scoring deterministic and consistent across sentences.
Reworked Examples: replaced/added examples that demonstrate the new modifiers (short PP comma, multiword-name split, restricting adverb) while keeping representative anchors for other key behaviors.
